title: Sharing That Doesn't Come Out Even

steps.body: Sharing does not stop when the numbers refuse to divide evenly. Three sandwiches among four people gives each three quarters — the leftover is cut, not abandoned.
steps.narration: Sharing does not stop when the numbers refuse to divide evenly. Three sandwiches among four people gives each three quarters — the leftover is cut, not abandoned.

widget.prompt: 3 sandwiches shared among 4 people. Build one person's share.
widget.successFeedback: 3/4 — each sandwich cut into fourths, and each person takes three of those pieces.
widget.lowFeedback: That build is SHORTER than 3/4 — either shade more pieces or make each piece larger until the lengths match.
widget.highFeedback: That build is LONGER than 3/4 — either shade fewer pieces or make each piece smaller until the lengths match.

commonFractions.feedback: 1/4 is one piece from ONE sandwich; there are three sandwiches to draw from.
4/3 is more than a whole sandwich each, which three cannot supply to four people.

predict.prompt: 3 shared among 4 — does anyone get a whole sandwich?
predict.reveal: Three wholes cannot give four people one each; every share must fall under a whole.

cml.actionGoal: Ask what is being cut and how big each piece is, then count the pieces for g5fd uneven share.
invariants: Division and fractions are the same act seen twice: sharing a wholes among b people gives a/b, and dividing BY a piece asks how many of it fit, which is why g5fd uneven share produces a larger answer when the divisor is under one.
misconceptions: Reading "divide by 1/4" as "take a quarter of", reporting a remainder when the leftover could be shared, or shrinking the pieces when only their count should change.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the divisor grew past one, would the answer become larger or smaller than the dividend?

widget.prompt: 3 sandwiches shared equally among 4 people. How much does each get?

options.label: 3/4 of a sandwich each
options.feedback: Correct — cut each sandwich into fourths and hand out three of them; a ÷ b is exactly a/b.

options.label: Nobody gets any, since 3 is less than 4
options.feedback: Sharing does not require whole items — the pieces simply come out smaller than one.

options.label: 4/3 of a sandwich
options.feedback: That is more than a whole sandwich each, which four people cannot get from only three.

options.label: 1 sandwich each, with one left over
options.feedback: That leaves the fourth person with nothing and wastes the remainder; equal sharing splits it.

steps.body: Every whole is split into as many pieces as there are people, and each person collects one piece from every whole.
steps.narration: Every whole is split into as many pieces as there are people, and each person collects one piece from every whole.

widget.prompt: 5 granola bars are shared among 6 hikers. Build one hiker's share.
widget.successFeedback: 5/6 — cut every bar into sixths; each hiker receives five sixth-size pieces.
widget.lowFeedback: That build is shorter than 5/6. Count one sixth from each of the five bars.
widget.highFeedback: That build is longer than 5/6. Six hikers cannot each receive a whole bar from five bars.

commonFractions.feedback: 1/6 uses a piece from only one bar; one share gets a sixth from each of five bars.
6/5 is greater than one, but five bars shared among six hikers gives less than one each.

widget.prompt: Compute 16 ÷ 8 — sharing 16 equal pieces among 8 people.

commonErrors.feedback: 16 is the WHOLE pile; the question asks what one of 8 equal shares holds.
Subtracting removes one share once; sharing equally is division.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Ask what is being cut and what size the pieces are; the count of pieces is the answer.

widget.prompt: Which fraction represents one person's share when 5 muffins are shared equally among 6 people?

options.label: 5/6 of a muffin
options.feedback: Correct — five wholes shared among six people gives 5 ÷ 6 = 5/6 to each person.

options.label: 6/5 of a muffin
options.feedback: 6/5 reverses the dividend and divisor and would give each person more than one muffin.

options.label: 1/6 of a muffin
options.feedback: 1/6 accounts for one muffin only; each person receives a sixth from all five muffins.

options.label: 5 muffins
options.feedback: Five muffins is the total amount being shared, not the amount one person receives.

concept.body: Every whole is split into as many pieces as there are people, and each person collects one piece from every whole.
concept.narration: Every whole is split into as many pieces as there are people, and each person collects one piece from every whole.

widget.prompt: A bar is split into 4 equal pieces. Mia receives 3 pieces. Which fraction of the bar does Mia receive?

options.feedback: Correct — the denominator counts four equal pieces and the numerator counts the three Mia receives.
4/3 swaps the counts. The whole was cut into four pieces, so 4 belongs on the bottom.
1/4 names one piece. Mia receives three of the four equal pieces.
Three is the number of pieces, but the answer must name their size as fourths.
